newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ITC Classic in revival plan.
newsitem.headline: India's ITC Classic in revival plan.

text.p: India's ITC Classic Finance Ltd, an affiliate of corporate giant ITC Ltd, on Monday approved a revival plan for the ailing company involving help from ITC.
A company spokesman said the firm's board had appointed Mukesh Palta as ITC Classic's new managing director in place of R. Chand, who would return to the management of the parent, ITC Ltd.

The company said in a statement its results were adversely affected by a liquidity crunch hurting the company's corporate clients, and unprecedented premature withdrawals of the company's fixed deposits between October 1996 and January 1997.

"Even though ITC Limited has no legal obligation to support such a revival package, as a responsible corporate citizen, ITC has given serious consideration to the proposal, in the larger interest of stabilising the non-banking finance company (NBFC) sector and thereby supporting orderly economic growth," it said.
ITC Classic reported a net loss of 2.85 billion rupees for 1996/97 (April-March), slipping into the red after reporting a net profit of 313.41 million rupees in the previous year.
The company's three-year revival package was prepared in consultation with its consortium of banks and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the statement said.
ITC's board had approved the package in principle, and further implementation was subject to approval by the consortium of banks of the revival plan, the statement said.
The statement gave no other details.

"ITC's intended support to Classic would be through injection of funds, strengthening of the company's management and, in due course, concluding an alliance with a partner of repute," the statement said.
Britain's B.A.T. Industries plc holds more than 31 percent of the equity of ITC Ltd, which has interests in cigarette-making, agribusiness and hoteliering.
